question_text: How many amendments does the U.S. Constitution have?

why_it_matters.text: The Constitution is hard to change on purpose. In over 230 years, Americans have agreed to update it just 27 times. Hard enough to protect the rules; possible enough to fix them when something really must change.

fun_fact.text: In 1982, a UT Austin sophomore named Gregory Watson wrote a paper arguing a forgotten amendment from 1789 could still be ratified. His professor gave him a C. He spent the next ten years pushing states to vote on it — and that C-grade paper became the 27th Amendment.
